original_value: Abstract The present paper studies so-called deep image prior (DIP) techniques in the context of ill-posed inverse problems. DIP networks have been recently introduced for applications in image processing; also first experimental results for applying DIP to inverse problems have DIP reported. This paper aims at discussing different interpretations of been and to obtain analytic results for specific network designs and linear operators. The main contribution is to introduce the idea of viewing these approaches as the optimization of Tikhonov functionals rather than optimizing networks. Besides theoretical results, we present numerical verifications.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines so-called deep image prior (DIP) methods in the setting of ill-posed inverse problems. Recently introduced for image-processing applications, DIP networks have also produced initial experimental results in inverse-problem settings. The paper discusses various interpretations and derives analytic results for particular network architectures and linear operators. Its principal contribution is the proposal to view these methods as minimizing Tikhonov functionals instead of optimizing networks. Along with theoretical findings, we also provide numerical verification.
